AbstractText.Label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To study the impact of uterine scar on pain experienced during outpatient hysteroscopy.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: A prospective blinded comparative study (Canadian Task Force classification II-1).

AbstractText.Label: SETTING
AbstractText.content: Outpatient hysteroscopy clinic at a university hospital.

AbstractText.Label: PATIENTS
AbstractText.content: We included 140 women in the childbearing period attending an outpatient hysteroscopy clinic. Patients were divided into 2 groups. Group A included patients with previous uterine scar (n = 70) and Group B included those with unscarred uterus (n = 70). None of the patients had a previous attempt of a vaginal delivery.

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTION
AbstractText.content: Diagnostic outpatient hysteroscopy without the use of anesthesia or analgesia.

AbstractText.Label: MEASUREMENTS
AbstractText.content: We assessed pain experienced during and immediately after the procedure using a 100-mm visual analog scale. We also evaluated the successful completion of the procedure.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: There were no statistically significant differences in the pain scores between patients with scarred uterus and those with unscarred uterus during or immediately after the procedure. The procedure was aborted in only 1 case in the scarred uterus group. This patient had a history of surgical site infection, which may denote a weak scar. There were no statistically significant differences in pain scores between patients with cesarean scar and those with myomectomy scar. No statistically significant differences in pain scores were found between patients with 1, 2, 3, or 4 cesarean deliveries.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Uncomplicated uterine scars do not have an impact on pain experienced during or immediately after diagnostic outpatient hysteroscopy using a 3.8-mm hysteroscope.
